---
title: "CRAN"
description: "For packages on CRAN: a waiting time between submissions, and the submission itself after a release."
---

Two optional workflows for a package that goes to CRAN. Both fit into the
[release chain](release.qmd) and do nothing harmful before the first
submission, so they can run there long before it.

## Waiting time

CRAN asks for updates of an established package no more often than every
one to two months. `cran-wait-check.yml` runs on the `dev` → `main` pull
request and fails it while the last CRAN submission is less than
`min-days` ago (60 by default; 90 for quarterly releases).

- **The last submission** is the later of the package's publication date
  on CRAN and the newest `cran-*` tag, which the submission below sets.
- **Not on CRAN yet:** the check passes.
- **An urgent fix:** the label `cran-hotfix` on the pull request lets it
  through; CRAN's policy allows urgent fixes.

Add it to the release trigger next to the R CMD check, and to the merge
job's `needs` and `if`, as in the commented job of the
[release trigger example](release.qmd#release-trigger).

## Submission

`cran-submit.yml` runs after the release (chained with `needs`): it checks
out the released commit, builds the package and uploads it with
`cran-comments.md` through CRAN's submission form, the steps of
`devtools::submit_cran()` without its questions. Then it tags the commit
`cran-<version>`.

- **CRAN emails the maintainer** (`cre` in `DESCRIPTION`), who confirms the
  submission. That step stays a person's.
- **`dry-run: true`** (the default) builds the package and shows what would
  be sent, and sends nothing. Keep it until the package is ready for CRAN:
  every release then rehearses the submission.
- **Before the first submission:** `R CMD check --as-cran` green on all
  three systems (the `as-cran` input of [R CMD check](r-cmd-check.qmd)),
  and a `cran-comments.md` in the package root.

See the commented `cran` job in the
[release publish example](release.qmd#publish-release).
